AppEntry.description:
One registered app.

Compiled-in apps and discovered WASM apps (N09) share this listing, and the
two carry different keys: everything a dynamic app does not have is
`Option`, and `runnable: false` with a `reason` is how a discovered module
this build cannot execute says so instead of vanishing from the list.

module_sha256.description: WASM apps only: the module digest, pinned in the catalog.

pinned.description: WASM apps only: the catalog pins this digest.

ready.description: Every requirement is satisfied on this node.

reason.description: WASM apps only, and only when not runnable.

requires.description: What this app needs before it can run, e.g. `env:CENSUS_API_KEY`.

runnable.description:
WASM apps only. `false` means listed but not executable here; enqueueing
it answers 409 with `reason`.

world.description: WASM apps only: the component world it exports.

AppReclaimDto.description: Retained artifact bytes for one app.

AppToolDefinition.description: One app as an agent-facing tool definition (`GET /apps?format=tools`).

inputSchema.description: JSON Schema for `params`; `{"type":"object"}` when the app declares none.

AppToolExample.description: One worked example an agent can copy.

AppToolsResponse.description: `GET /apps?format=tools` — the same registry as tool definitions.

evidence_sha.description:
The digest of the evidence bundle the approver actually read
(`input_request.evidence_sha`, also on `GET /transactions/{id}`).

Optional, and a mismatch is a refusal. Quoting it is how an approval
proves it is an approval *of something*: a client that re-fetched the
row after a re-stage refreshed the evidence would otherwise release an
action against a bundle nobody looked at.

AppsResponse.description:
`GET /apps`: the registry, or the same apps as agent tool definitions with
`?format=tools`.

AuditEntryDto.description: One audit entry: a mutating verb, who did it, and to what.

detail.description: A raw JSON STRING, not an object.

principal_id.description: `null` in `open` mode — the action is still logged, without a caller.

batch.description: Rows per keyset batch (clamped to 1..=1000; default 500).

cursor.description:
Resume point from a previous response's `cursor`. Absent starts over —
which is always safe, the work is idempotent per row.

max_rows.description:
Rows this request may scan before it stops and returns a `cursor`
(default 50000). Aggregate specs treat it as a hard ceiling instead:
they need one full pass, so exceeding it is a 400 that writes nothing.

app.description: Restrict the batch to one app.

CacheKeyFreshness.description: One cache key's learned change cadence.

last_change_at.description: `null` when it has never been seen to change.

CallerPrincipalDto.description: Who the server resolved this request as.

synthetic.description:
True in `[auth] mode = "open"`: the synthetic operator, not a stored
principal. Saying so is what keeps "unauthenticated" from reading as
"authenticated as somebody".

CancelJobResponse.description:
`DELETE /jobs/{id}`.

Three shapes share this schema, which is why everything but `cancelled` is
optional: a queued job answers `{cancelled: true}`; a running one adds
`running: true`; and a job that lost the race with a graceful shutdown —
it had already committed to a checkpoint suspend — answers
`{cancelled: false, running: true, suspended: true, note}`. That last one is
not a cancellation at all, and saying so honestly is the point.

note.description: ABSENT unless `suspended`; explains what happened instead.

running.description: ABSENT unless the job was in flight.

suspended.description: ABSENT unless the job was re-queued by the shutdown drain instead.

see_also.description: Pointer to the sibling endpoint answering the other health question.

CatalogHealthSource.description: One source's freshness verdict — did it RUN, as against did it run right.

contract.description:
The declared contract plus its last verdict; ABSENT when none is
declared.

last_write_at.description: `null` when the dataset has never been written.

monitored.description: `false` when this source has no freshness expectation to check against.

reason.description: Why it is unmonitored, or why it is considered stale. ABSENT otherwise.

CatalogSourceDto.description: One catalog `[[source]]` — the machine-readable pipeline registry row.

oneOf.description: ABSENT when the source declares no contract.

capabilities.description:
The apps this executor offers to run. Empty = "whatever you'll give me".
Always intersected with the coordinator's executor-eligible set, so it
can only narrow.

executor_id.description:
This executor's stable identity. Stamped onto the claimed row and
required by every later write about it.

ClaimedJob.description:
One claimed job, as the executor needs it: everything `AppContext`
construction takes, and nothing the coordinator keeps to itself (no callback
secret, no principal, no resumed-input on a job that never parked).

attempt.description:
The attempt number this claim advanced to — the fence value for every
write about this job.

budget_usd.description:
The budget the coordinator resolved (including a DataHub `cost:pause`
forcing `$0`), not the raw enqueue value.

restored.description:
The last durable checkpoint, if the job has one, run through the same
poisoned-checkpoint escape the local worker applies.

resumed_input.description: The answer a `POST /jobs/{id}/resume` stored for a previously parked job.

grants.description:
The unified record's `data` spread inline, plus a guaranteed `key` and
`days_left`. Rows whose `close_date` will not parse are DROPPED rather
than given a fabricated deadline.

ranges.description: Field name to a `{min, max}` bound.

types.description: Field name to expected JSON type.

ContractsStatusDto.description:
Whether declared data contracts are being enforced, and whether the catalog
that declares them could even be read.

catalog_error.description: ABSENT when the catalog read succeeded.

enforce_observed.description:
What the worker ACTUALLY did, which is the number that matters: a
configured gate that never observed is not a gate.

principal.description: Echo of `?principal=`; `null` when the ledger was not restricted.

CostSummaryRow.description: One `(app, engine)` row of the spend ledger.

group_by.description:
Aggregate spec (v2): `$.path` group keys. Requires `aggregates`;
mutually exclusive with `lookup` and `project`.

source_app.description: App namespace the source AND the derived dataset live in.

target_dataset.description: Dataset the shaped rows are upserted into (same app).

secret.description: Signing secret; generated (and returned ONCE) when omitted.

budget_usd_per_day.description:
Daily spend ceiling in USD across every job this key enqueues. Omitted =
**no ceiling**, the same convention `budget_usd` uses at every other
door — so `0`/negative is refused rather than reinterpreted.

rate_limit_per_min.description:
Requests/minute (also the burst). Omitted = the `[auth]`
`default_rate_limit_per_min` fallback.

scopes.description:
Scope strings: `"admin"`, `"read"`, `"enqueue:<app>"`, `"enqueue:*"`.
An unknown scope is a 400, never a silently powerless key.

app.description: Optional scope: only this app / dataset.

oneOf.description:
If set, each run also snapshots the query's result set into this dataset
(M13 "queries as datasets"): one record per hit keyed by search doc id,
hits that fall out of the results tombstoned — so the view's deltas feed
watches/triggers/`?filter=`/export. Capped by `[search]
max_materialize_results`.

secret.description: If set, delivery bodies are HMAC-SHA256 signed with this secret.

url.description: Webhook that receives `search.matched` events for NEW matches.

budget_usd.description:
Spend ceiling replayed into **every** job this schedule enqueues; metered
Claude calls abort past it. Must be **> 0** — validated by the same
`jobs::validate_budget_usd` the enqueue and trigger doors use, so `0`,
negative, NaN and ∞ are refused with the identical 422 rather than
silently becoming "no ceiling". Omitted = no ceiling (unchanged
behaviour, and the only thing catalog-managed schedules can have).

cron.description: 6-field cron with seconds: "sec min hour day month weekday".

max_attempts.description: Attempt budget for jobs this schedule enqueues; omitted = server default (3).

misfire_policy.description:
Catch-up policy for firings missed while the scheduler was down:
"fire_once" (default) runs a single job; "skip" runs none.

params.description:
Params for the jobs this schedule enqueues. An object **shallow-merges
over the app's `default_params`**, exactly like `POST /apps/{name}/jobs`
— so setting one key keeps the rest of the defaults. Validated here
against the app's declared schema (422), on the merged result.

timezone.description:
IANA timezone the cron is evaluated in (e.g. "America/New_York"); omitted
= UTC. An unknown name is rejected with 400 `bad_request`.

from_seq.description:
Where the cursor starts. Omitted = **now**: the subscription receives
what happens next, not the retained backlog. `0` replays the whole
retained log — which is the point of a durable cursor, and is also a
burst, so it is opt-in rather than the default.

name.description: Operator-facing label. Not an identity — the id is.

secret.description: HMAC-SHA256 signing secret for delivery bodies. Never read back.

selector.description:
`{kinds: [..], app, dataset, filters: [{pointer, equals}]}`. Every field
narrows; `{}` (or omitted) subscribes to the whole log.

url.description: The delivery endpoint (or, for a `plugin:` sink, the connector's target).

bind.description:
N04 param binding: `{"<target param>": "<JSON pointer>"}` resolved
against the `{template, _trigger}` view BEFORE the target-schema door,
so the event can steer the target's own params (`{"url":
"/_trigger/payload/repository/html_url"}`) instead of only riding under
`_trigger`. A pointer that resolves to nothing is the ledger outcome
`bind_miss` and the hop is not enqueued.

budget_usd.description:
The TARGET's spend ceiling (never inherited from the source). Must be
**> 0** — see `jobs::validate_budget_usd`: omitting it means "no
ceiling", so `0` cannot also mean "spend nothing" and is refused (422).
Worse here than at the jobs door: the value is stored on the trigger row
and replayed into EVERY hop it fires, so a silently-dropped `0` would be
a standing unlimited-spend generator, not one bad job.

each.description:
N04 per-record fan-out: a JSON pointer to an ARRAY in that same view.
One hop per element, each carrying `_trigger.item` / `item_index` /
`fan_out_total` / `fan_out_truncated`, capped by `[triggers]
fan_out_cap`.

filters.description:
External kind only: `$.path:op:value` predicate specs (the `?filter=`
grammar) ANDed against the inbound payload.

params.description: Static params template; `_trigger` is merged over it at fire time.

plugins.description:
Sandboxed WASM hooks (M15): `predicate` returns fire/skip over the
`_trigger` delta envelope (`{"pass": bool}`, fail-open per `on_error`),
`transform` shapes the `_trigger` object before target params. Any
source kind. The named plugin need not be loaded yet (hot reload);
a missing plugin at fire time takes the fail-open path, loudly.

source_app.description: External kind: an ingress source id or '*' (any source).

source_dataset.description: Dataset kind only: dataset name or '*' (default).

app.description:
The app **namespace** the records land under — which is not always the
app that produced them. Registered apps, plus the virtual namespaces the
change fan-out delivers under (e.g. `grants`, which is where every grant
source's unified records go).

dataset.description: Dataset to watch; "*" (default) watches every dataset of the app.

secret.description:
If set, delivery bodies are HMAC-SHA256 signed with this secret
(webhook sink; Slack ignores the signature header, file sinks are local).

sink.description:
Delivery connector: "webhook" (default), "file" (NDJSON append under
data/sinks/), or "slack" (incoming-webhook message at `url`).

url.description:
Delivery target. `webhook`/`slack` sinks: required, the URL POSTed at.
`file` sink: ignored — the file is always `data/sinks/<watch_id>.ndjson`.

cron.description:
Optional 5/6-field cron. Present = the scheduler fires a run per firing,
held while the newest run of this plan is still open.

name.description:
Unique, human-chosen name. Also accepted wherever an id is, so callers
can `POST /workflows/nightly-refresh/runs`.

spec.description:
`{steps: {name: {app, params?, after?, budget_usd?, priority?,
max_attempts?}}, budget_usd?, on_failure?}`.

DatahubStatusResponse.description:
`GET /datahub/status` — DataHub and OpenLineage emission state.

Free-form on purpose: the block is assembled from the emitters' own
counters, the governance poller's last summary and per-writer lineage
status, all of which change with those subsystems rather than with this
route. Its keys are `enabled`, `gms_url`, `env`, `token_set`, `emit_schema`,
`emit_profile`, `emit_flows`, `last_emission`, `emissions`, `govern` and
`lineage`.

DatahubSyncResponse.description:
`POST /datahub/sync` — one emission's outcome. `entities` on success and
`error` on failure are mutually exclusive.

datasets.description: ABSENT when the run failed before listing datasets.

trust.description: Echo of `?trust=` — which trust levels this feed was restricted to.

DatasetDeletion.description:
`DELETE /datasets/{app}/{dataset}` once confirmed.

The unconfirmed call answers 428 with a preview instead — deleting a dataset
is the one irreversible door here, so the confirmation is part of the
contract rather than a nicety.

deleted.description:
Equal to `records`; kept for the consumers that read it before
`records` existed.

export.description: Where the pre-delete NDJSON snapshot was written.

preview.description: Always `false` on the 200 — the 428 preview is where `true` appears.

DatasetManifest.description:
`GET /datasets/{app}/{dataset}/manifest` — the digest a mesh peer reconciles
against.

complete.description:
`false` when the dataset is larger than `cap`: the digest then covers a
prefix, and a peer must not treat a mismatch as a ghost.

digest.description: SHA-256 over the sorted live keys.

live_count.description: Live keys only — the set the digest covers.

DeletedResponse.description: `{deleted: true}` — the answer every idempotent delete door gives.

DeliveryDto.description: One delivery attempt of a webhook / watch / subscription sink.

body.description:
ABSENT on list rows (those queries select an empty body, which the core
struct skips); populated on `GET /webhooks/deliveries/{id}`.

cursor.description: ABSENT when `done` — the resume token for the next pass.

DerivedDeleted.description:
`DELETE /derived/{id}` — answers with the id, not a bool, unlike the other
delete doors. Kept as served.

DerivedGroupDto.description: The `group` clause of a derived spec.

DerivedLookupDto.description: The `lookup` clause of a derived spec.

DoctorArtifacts.description:
The doctor's artifact scan; `{scanned: false}` and nothing else when
`?skip_artifacts=true`, so every other field is optional.

examples.description: A handful of offending rows, shape depending on the check.

severity.description: `warn` | `info`. The doctor never blocks, so there is no `error`.

read_only.description: Always `true`. This endpoint deletes nothing, ever.

store.description:
The SQLite store instrument's own report — latency percentiles per
operation, file sizes, pool saturation and the maintenance ledger. Its
shape is owned by `pumper_core::store_instrument` and changes with the
instrument, so it is deliberately not pinned here.

DoctorSearch.description: Whether the search index and the store agree about how much exists.

doc_count.description: `null` when the index could not be read — unknown, not zero.

DoctorTable.description: One append-only table and the retention that is (or is not) bounding it.

DoctorThresholds.description:
The doctor's `thresholds` block: the constants its verdicts were judged by,
so a reader can tell a finding from a policy.

DupPairDto.description: One near-duplicate pair and its SimHash Hamming distance.

max_distance.description: The CLAMPED distance actually used, which may be below what was asked.

EconomicsApp.description: One app's economics inside one window.

EconomicsClaude.description: Claude spend for one app in one window, and whether it paid for itself.

records_per_dollar.description:
`null` together with `worth_it` when there was no Claude spend or the
yield is unknown.

EconomicsDataset.description: One dataset's yield inside an economics window.

EconomicsWindow.description: One rolling window of the economics report.

EconomicsWindows.description: The two windows the report always carries.

EnabledResponse.description: `{id, enabled}` — the answer every `POST .../enabled` toggle gives.

EnforcementPreview.description:
`GET /enforcement/preview` — what `[resilience] enforce = true` would have
done. Gates nothing, writes nothing.

budget_usd.description:
Spend ceiling for the whole job; metered Claude calls abort past it.
Must be **> 0** — see [`validate_budget_usd`]: omitting it means "no
ceiling", so `0` cannot also mean "spend nothing" and is refused (422)
rather than silently reinterpreted as unlimited.

callback_secret.description: If set, the callback body is HMAC-SHA256 signed with this secret.

callback_url.description: POST the finished job here on terminal state.

idempotency_key.description:
Dedup key: retrying an enqueue with the same key returns the original
job (200) instead of creating a duplicate. The `Idempotency-Key`
header takes precedence over this field.

params.description:
Job params. An object here **shallow-merges over the app's
`default_params`** (see `GET /apps`), so setting one key keeps the rest of
the defaults — matching what the scheduler runs. A non-object value
replaces the defaults wholesale.

ErrorEnvelope.description:
The error envelope every 4xx/5xx carries (`routes::error::ApiError`).

`code` is the stable machine token clients branch on; `error` is the human
sentence, which is NOT stable and must never be parsed.

error.description: Human-readable message. Not a contract — do not match on it.

EventLogPage.description: `GET /events/log` — the pull page of the event log.

latest_seq.description: The log's head, so `latest_seq - after` is your backlog.

next_after.description:
Send as `after` next time; `null` when the page did not fill, i.e. you
are caught up and should back off rather than spin.

pending.description: Events buffered but not yet drained to their sinks.

retained.description:
Rows still retained — the log is pruned past `[events]
log_retention_days`, so this is not the number ever written.

EventRecordDto.description: One row of the durable event log.

seq.description:
Monotonic sequence — the cursor. Survives a restart, and is the same
number `Last-Event-ID` carries on the SSE streams.

subject_id.description: Job id, dataset name, transaction id — whatever this kind is about.

saved.description: `false` when the checkpoint was refused (e.g. the job moved on).

ExecutorFinishResponse.description: `POST /jobs/{id}/finish` — what the coordinator did with the report.

eligible_apps.description:
Which apps this plane may claim, so an executor that never gets work can
tell a capability mismatch from an empty queue.

ExecutorWrite.description:
What every executor-driven write names: the job's attempt and the executor
that claims to hold it. Both are required — the attempt is the fence the
local worker already lives under, and the executor id is what makes a
*reaped* process's late write refusable rather than merely unlucky.

attempt.description: The attempt this executor was handed. Must equal `jobs.attempts`.

error.description: `finish`: the failure, when it did not. Exactly one of `result`/`error`.

executor_id.description: The executor reporting. Must equal `jobs.executor_id` for this row.

result.description: `finish`: the job result, when the run succeeded.

run_ms.description:
`finish`: how long the app's own `run()` took on the executor, so the
coordinator's stage row is not silently missing the only span it cannot
measure. Optional; absent means unmeasured, never zero.

ExtractPreviewResponse.description: `POST /extract/preview` — a RuleSet dry run against one document.

report.description:
Per-field extraction status, coercion outcomes and `each` sub-stats. Its
shape follows the RuleSet the caller sent, so it is free-form here.

values.description: The extracted record. Keys are the caller's own rule fields.

FetchProxyResponse.description:
`POST /fetch-proxy` — one fetch performed through this node's local stack on
a peer's behalf.

headers.description:
Response headers, plus one this node adds naming the URL it was asked
for — so a caller can tell which request an answer belongs to.

GovernDisableSchedule.description: A schedule the governance poll would disable.

suppressed.description: True when the action is suppressed by policy and would NOT be taken.

GovernEnqueueSync.description: A sync the governance poll would enqueue.

registered.description: False when no such app is registered here — the action would be a no-op.

GovernTotals.description: Counts of what the poll would do.

GovernWould.description: Everything the governance poll would do.

GovernancePreview.description:
`GET /datahub/governance/preview` — what the poll would do right now.
Writes nothing.

quiet.description: True when the poll found nothing to say.

read_errors.description:
Datasets whose governance metadata could not be read. A read error is
NOT an absence of policy, which is why `poll_would_abort` exists.

status.description: Always `ok` — the endpoint answering at all IS the liveness signal.

HostProfileDto.description: One host's learned tier memory and politeness penalty.

observations.description: ABSENT on the live-penalty-only answer for a host with no stored row.

penalty_ms.description: The LIVE governor delay, not the stored one.

preferred_tier.description: The tier the router pins for this host; `null` when it has learned none.

HostWeatherExport.description:
`GET /host-weather/export`: the signed v2 envelope, or the unsigned legacy
flat bundle with `?schema=1`.

HostWeatherImportResponse.description:
`POST /host-weather/import`. An import only ever RAISES local caution — it
cannot make this node less polite than it already decided to be.

schema.description: Echoed from the bundle; empty string when it declared none.

HostWeatherLegacyBundle.description:
`GET /host-weather/export?schema=1` — the legacy flat bundle, which is
UNSIGNED. Kept so an older peer keeps working; new consumers should read the
signed `SignedBundle` the default answer carries.

node_id.description: The LEGACY id, not the ed25519 node id.

seq.description: The log sequence this event landed at.

IngressSourceCreated.description: `POST /ingress/sources` — the only response that ever carries the secret.

secret.description: Shown ONCE. It is stored hashed and can never be read back.

IngressSourceDto.description: One inbound webhook source. `secret` is returned exactly once, at creation.

fresh_records.description:
`null` when the job has no result yet — an unknown yield, never a
fabricated zero.

progress.description:
ABSENT (not null) unless the job is running and the worker has published
a snapshot. In-memory only — it does not survive a restart.

JobDetail.description: `GET /jobs/{id}`: a job plus, for a running one, its live progress snapshot.

JobDto.description:
One queued/running/finished job (`pumper_core::Job`). `callback_secret` and
`resumed_input` are `skip_serializing` on the core struct and are absent from
the wire, so they are absent here.

input_request.description: What a `waiting` job is waiting for (N02).

JobPage.description: `GET /jobs` without `cursor` is a bare `[Job]`; with it, this envelope.

oneOf.description: `null` when no stage row was recorded for this attempt.

unknown.description:
What this receipt could NOT establish, in prose. Never empty in
practice — the honest-absence half of the contract.

JobsResponse.description: `GET /jobs`: bare `[Job]`, or a keyset page with `?cursor=`.

LookupBody.description: Body twin of core's [`DerivedLookup`] (which doesn't carry a utoipa schema).

key_expr.description: `$.path` into the SOURCE record that yields the lookup key.

merge_as.description: Field of the derived row the looked-up record is merged under.

MarketProfileResponse.description:
`GET /market/profile/{state}/{trade}` — the record's `data`, unwrapped.

The row is an app-owned cross-family join (economics x density) whose blocks
evolve with the apps that write it, so the payload is free-form here rather
than a schema this route does not enforce. `coverage` is `both` or
`economics_only`, and `density` is `null` for the latter — an absent join,
never a fabricated density.

app.description: App namespace the view dataset lives under (e.g. `search`).

node_id.description: Empty string when this node's identity could not be read.

MeshStream.description: One sync stream with one peer.

lag_secs.description: Seconds since the last SUCCESS; `null` when there has never been one.

scheduled.description:
False when the schedule for this stream does not exist — the stream is
configured but nothing is pulling it.

signature_failures.description:
Non-zero here means a peer's bundles are being rejected, silently as far
as the data is concerned.

key_created.description: True when this request is what created the key.

plugins.description:
Each plugin's SELF-DECLARED manifest. The host does not impose a shape
on it, so neither does this schema.

base_url.description:
The document's own URL, which `url_absolute` transforms resolve relative
links against. Defaults to `url` when fetching; supply it with `html` to
preview a rule set against a body you pasted in. Without it a rule set
using `url_absolute` still runs, but the report says `base_url_missing`.

html.description:
Inline document to run the rules against. Provide exactly one of
`html` or `url`.

rules.description:
A `RuleSet`: a bare `{field: rule}` map (the same shape apps take), e.g.
`{"title": {"type": "css", "selector": "h1"}}`.

url.description:
URL to fetch (HTTP tier only — no browser/Claude escalation) and run the
rules against. Provide exactly one of `html` or `url`.

PreviewConsequencesDto.description: What enforcement WOULD have done, counted per consequence.

PreviewNotReady.description: One source that is NOT ready for enforcement, and which gates it fails.

oneOf.description: ABSENT when there is no transition to point at.

PreviewRunCount.description: Runs and documents one consequence would have touched.

live_state.description: The state the LIVE system is in, as against the replayed one.

unjudged_runs.description: Runs the judge could not score — the honest denominator.

window_opens_at.description: ABSENT when the window is already open.

PreviewTransitionDto.description: One state transition the replay would have made.

principal_id.description:
`null` is the unattributed bucket — spend from before N20 stamped a
principal, or from an `open`-mode operator.

PrincipalCreated.description: `POST /principals` — the only response that carries a new key.

key.description: Shown ONCE. Stored only as a digest and never readable again.

PrincipalDto.description:
One API principal. `key_hash` is never serialized, and the plaintext key
exists in exactly two responses: creation and rotation.

oneOf.description: `null` when no principal was resolved for this request.

PrincipalRotated.description: `POST /principals/{id}/rotate` — the old key stops working immediately.

ProfileInfoDto.description: One named login profile. Cookies and browser state are never returned.

ProfileListResponse.description: `GET /profiles` — the session vault's named login profiles.

ProposalPromotion.description:
`POST /provisioner/proposals/{key}/promote` — hands back the catalog block
to paste. This route NEVER writes `catalog/data-sources.toml` itself.

catalog_toml.description: A TOML `[[source]]` fragment, as a string.

ProposalSummary.description: One compiled proposal awaiting validation or promotion.

expired.description: A proposal past its freshness window: its sample no longer stands.

ProposalValidation.description:
`POST /provisioner/proposals/{key}/validate` — a real fetch and a real dry
run, with the verdict written back onto the proposal.

validation.description:
`{checked_at, sample, dry_run, accepted}` — the sample statistics and the
held-out dry run, both owned by the provisioner app.

ProposalsResponse.description: `GET /provisioner/proposals`: bare array, or a keyset page.

ProvenanceCoverage.description: How much of a record's history can be replayed.

replayable.description:
Revisions holding BOTH an archived body and a rules hash — the ones
`rederive` can actually re-run.

ProvenanceJob.description: The job that wrote one revision; `null` when the id is unknown or unparseable.

ProvenanceLink.description: One link of a record's derivation chain.

ProvenanceStamp.description: The derivation stamp on one revision.

ReceiptArtifacts.description:

delete.description:
This route used to destroy every record and its full revision history on a
bare `DELETE`, with no echo, no preview and no receipt — the single most
destructive verb in the API, reachable by a stale browser tab or a copied
curl line. Three rungs now stand in front of it, in cost order (registry:
data-retention/confirm-by-echo, "echo is one rung of a ladder"):

1. **Preview.** Without both parameters the call counts and returns 428.
   Nothing is written, and the payload says `preview: true` so a saved
   response can never be read as proof of a deletion.
2. **The echo** (`confirm=<app>/<dataset>`). Its honest value is narrow and
   worth stating: `app` and `dataset` are already in the path, so this rung
   proves intent, not comprehension — it is what makes an accidental bare
   `DELETE` inert. It is compared against the identity the store resolved
   (`counts.app`/`counts.dataset`, the strings the `WHERE` clause binds),
   trimmed, exactly.
3. **The yield guard** (`expect_records=<n>`). This is the rung that measures
   comprehension: `n` cannot be known without having read the target, and it
   is re-checked inside the deleting transaction, so a population that moved
   between the preview and the delete is a 409 rather than a surprise.

Authentication is a fourth rung this server cannot climb: it has no identity
concept at all (the only credential anywhere is the ingress HMAC, which
authenticates a webhook *sender*, not an operator). That gap is recorded in
`.ai/registry-conformance.md` rather than papered over with an invented
scheme — these rungs contain the accident, not an attacker on the port.

Before anything is destroyed, every record and every revision is written to
an NDJSON export under `artifacts_dir/deleted-datasets/`, and its path is in
the receipt. If that write fails, nothing is deleted.
